The CLERK reported that he had received a communica- tion on this subj. cf, in which he information tendered by Mr. Whitlow at the last meeting, to the effect that the rail- company were about to bring water from their well at Acton Bridge, was contradicted. The other business before the meeting was not of public interest.

div.head: WIDNES POLICE COMM
div.p: WIDNES POLICE COMM
WEDNESDAY.—Before Mfgsr3. Holbrook Gaslien, Sen., and
S. H. Hall.

DrtuNlK Of LICENSED PEEMISES.—A young man, named Ephraim Uoatsworth, was charged with being drunk on licensed premises. On Thursday, the Bth inst., the defendant entered the Ditton public-house, Ditton, in a state of intoxi- cation, and insisted upon being served with whisky. 'The landlord refused to do so, and the defendant was ejected.— He was fined ss. and costs.

TIIE COMMENCEMENT OF CRIME. - John Carrott and James Taylor were charged with playing at pitch and toss in Water-street, on Sunday, tile 4th inst.—The Chairman said boys commenced by playing pitch and toss on Sunday, and went on to worse crimes. Each defendant was fined Is. and 4s. costs.

ASSAULT BY A WOMAN.—Catherine Stanton, a married woman, was summoned by Ann Feeley.—The complainant stated that on Saturday night the defendant went to her door, and arter a short conversation, took from the ground a handful of "clutch " and threw it "between her eyes," covering her all over. On the Sunday night the defendant threw Cricks and mortar in the house, and used threatening language.—Defendant called for the defence her daturhter, who, however, admitted her mother had committed the assault under provocation.—Defendant said although she had been in Widnes 20 veers she had never been before the Bench before.—The Superintendent observed that this was not quite correct as she had been up seven times.—The Chairman : You inget pay a fine of 10e. and costs, or go to prison for 14 dlys.-13:4endant : All right, sir. A GIRL COMMITTED FOR TRIAL.—A girl, named Annie Maria Adams, was brought up charged with stealing an alarum clock, of the value of 55., from the dwelling-house of John O'Donnell, living at 23, Hutchinson-street. Widnes. The robbery was alleged to have been committed on the 13th February. It appeared that on the evening of that day the prosecutor left home, leaving the back door unlocked, and no one in charge of the premises. The clock was then on the mantel pieee in the kitchen, but when the prosecutor re- turned within an hour, be discovered the clock had been re- moved, and be had not seen it until the previous day when it was shown to him by P.S. Robinson.—Ann O'Donnell, the wife of the prosecutor, gave evidence confirmatory of this statement, and in reply to the prisoner said she had ordered her to pawn "things" for her, but did not think she was dishonest.—The prisoner had stated to P.S. Johnson that she had found it in the back yard.—The Superintendent said the mother of the prisoner stated she was unable to do any good with her.—The prisoner, who had been previously convicted of stealing coal, was committed to the Sessions for trial. ALLEGED BIGAMY BY A WIDNES WOMAN.—Elizabeth Kerr, a middle-tged woman, was placed in the dock on a charge of bigamy.—Superintendent Barker said the prisoner bad been apprehended, under a warrant, charged with that she did feloniously marry and take to husband John Harbi- son t n the 26th November, 1881, John Kerr, to whom she was previously married on the 16th September, 1867, being then alive. He was not prepared to go on with the case, and he asked for a remand until to-morrow at Prescot. The witnesses, with one exception, lived in St. Helene.—Mr. Beasley, who appeared for the prisoner, applied for her to be admitted to b til.—The application was granted. A STREET Row: THE POLICE PELTED.—Wm. Hewitt, a labourer, was charged on remand with being drunk and dis- orderly, and also with assaultine P.C. Hanson, in Travis, on the evening of Friday, the 9th inst.—P.C. Hanson deposed that at that time the prisoner was creating a dis- turbance, at d a crowd of about 500 people assembled. The prisoner struck a man named 'Mulvey, and the witness then seized him with the intention of taking him home. A struggle ensued, ant the prisoner severely bit the censtable's hand and attempted to throw him down. P.C. Ormerod then arrived on the scene, and the prisoner was taken in custody. When conveying him to the police station, the crowd followed and pelted the constables with bricks and stones.— Mr. Be tslev, who appeared for the prisoner, cross-examined the consteble, who stated the prisoner's face was bleeding.— Three witnesses gave corroborative evidence, and Mr. Beas- ley addressed the Bench for the defence.—The prisoner had been several times previously convicted, and he was fined 5s and costs for being drank, and 20s and costs for the assault upon the police.—Wm. Hewitt, the prisoner in the last case, then charged Edward Mulvay with assaulting him on the same evening, and Mrs. Mulvey was charged with asseul ing Ellen Hewitt.—Mr. Beasley appeared for the complainants.—lt appeared that Hewitt and Mulvey had same grievance respecting a cart, and the latter struck the former with his fist. This caused a tight, in which the wives of the two men jeined. The police arrived, and Hewitt committed an assault on them.—The witnesses having been heard, El ward Mulvey was fined is and costs, and the case against Mrs. Ilu'vay dismissed.

EXTENSIVE THEFT' OF CLOTIIING.—EIiZabeth Scott was c.hargd with stealinL4. a large quantity of wearing apparel from the house of Francis Cook, a labourer, living at 4, Poole-street, Widnes.—The prisoner and her husband took apartments at the prosecutor's house in December, 1870, and had retained them until the 12th inst. When they had departed Mr. Cook missed a table cloth, and making a search she disc Nvered a large quantity of clothing was also missing. There was found, however, in a tea pot, a number of pawn tickets relating to articles pledged by the prisoner at Mrs. Jameson's. She went to the shop, and identified the greater part of the articles as her property. They were valued at about PA 10s.—Mrs. Jameson gave evidence as to the prisoner pawning the articles, and she was then committed to take her trial at the ssions.

ROBBRILY FROM THE ROYAL OAK PUBLICHOrSII.-11lph Wilson was charged with stealing 4s.r the moneypf Wm. Bailey Cross, from the Royal Oak public-house.—Proseco- tor said that the same morning, about half-past twelve, the prisoner came to the bar and was supplied with a small quantity of whiskey. He went out and left Wilson thorn. and immediately afterwards heard the till drawer rattle. He ran into the room and found the prisoner with 4s. in his hand.—Prisoner now pleaded guilty, and was sent to gao) for one month with hard. labour.
